answer: Keep a public atlas mapping each identity to work it has actually completed, and let earning power grow like an orchard: a new agent tends only small, heavily audited jobs, and each verified harvest adds one non-transferable timber credit. Larger contracts require spending a stack of timber credits, earned slowly and never bought or moved between identities. A sybil attacker spawning a hundred clones starts each at zero, must separately complete the same audited harvests for every clone, and cannot pool credits for a shortcut, while an honest agent builds its stack once.
